title: Abuja courtroom jails fraudster 7 years for defrauding American $205,238
text:
The {Economic} and {Financial} Crimes Commission (EFCC), has secured the conviction and sentence of Nwachi Chidozie Kingsley for acquiring $205,238 from an American, Nicole Kierulff Sayers, below false pretence.
Justice U.P. Kekemeke of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Excessive Court, Maitama, Abuja, convicted Kingsley on Thursday, October 29, 2026, and sentenced him to seven years’ imprisonment on every of the 2 counts, with out an possibility of high-quality.
The sentences are to run concurrently at Kuje Correctional Centre, Abuja.
The courtroom additionally ordered Kingsley to restitute the sufferer the sum of $205,238 (Two Hundred and 5 Thousand, Two Hundred and Thirty-Eight United States {Dollars}).
Kingsley was prosecuted by the EFCC on a two-count amended cost bordering on possession of a doc containing false pretence and acquiring cash by false pretence in reference to a purported contract with the Federal Ministry of Works and Housing.
One of many fees accused him of being in possession of a faux discover of intent to award a contract, allegedly issued in his title by the Ministry. The second rely accused him of acquiring $205,238 from Sayers below the false pretence that the cash was required to finance a authorities contract, realizing that the declare was false.
Whereas testifying earlier than the courtroom, Sayers, an American lawyer primarily based within the state of Oregon, United States, recognized Kingsley as the person who contacted her on Fb on her birthday.
“I do know the defendant. The defendant messaged me on Fb on my birthday and he mentioned he was a member of the identical religious group as me,” she advised the courtroom.
Based on her, their conversations developed right into a romantic relationship, which she mentioned made her belief him and consider his claims.
Sayers advised the courtroom that Kingsley subsequently requested her for cash to facilitate the award of a contract by the Federal Ministry of Works and Housing. He allegedly claimed that some males had been threatening his life as a result of he had not supplied the cash required to safe the contract.
She mentioned Kingsley equipped her with particulars of the purported contract, together with a brand and different data, which she believed as a result of she had developed an emotional attachment to him.
The witness additional testified that Kingsley initially requested $15,000, promising to repay the cash inside 45 days. She transferred the cash to him via a cash switch utility.
Based on Sayers, Kingsley subsequently launched her to members of his household throughout a video call, throughout which they allegedly thanked her for serving to him safe the purported contract.
She advised the courtroom that she had transferred roughly $40,000 to Kingsley earlier than travelling to Nigeria to satisfy him in particular person.
Sayers mentioned she arrived in Abuja March 2022 and spent two weeks with the defendant at his rented home in Solar Metropolis, Abuja. She claimed that she continued the connection as a result of she wished to get well her cash.
The witness additional alleged that Kingsley subsequently requested further funds for numerous functions, together with medical emergencies, surgical procedures, malaria remedy and provides for the purported authorities contract.
She advised the courtroom that the requests concerned greater than 125 transactions and that the entire quantity she transferred was, by her estimate, nicely over $200,000 inside a 12-month interval.
Sayers additionally testified that Kingsley offered her with a doc he claimed was proof that he had tried to switch $10,000 to her.
Based on her, he claimed that the {bank} had intercepted the transaction as a result of the cash was allegedly linked to the misappropriation of presidency funds, which he mentioned had resulted in his arrest and detention.
She additional alleged that Kingsley requested her to supply cash for his bail and for bribes linked to the purported legal case.
Sayers advised the courtroom that she repeatedly requested Kingsley to refund her cash. Based on her, he finally requested her {bank} particulars and promised to switch the cash the next day, however failed to take action.
She mentioned she later realised that he wouldn’t repay the cash.
On the conclusion of the prosecution’s case, counsel for the EFCC, Fatsuma Muhammad, urged the courtroom to convict and sentence the defendant in accordance with the regulation.
In his judgment, Justice Kekemeke discovered Kingsley responsible and sentenced him to imprisonment with out an possibility of high-quality, with the phrases of imprisonment to run concurrently.
